text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- Howden Sirocco desulphurisation equipment maker has contracted Mostostal Stalowa Wola construction firm to install two 200-tonnes heating components of the Polaniec power plant desulphurisation facility.

- A group of far eastern shipyards have produced their tender offers to the Szczecin-based Polska Zegluga Baltycka (PZM) shipping firm which plans to acquire five bulk-carriers to operate on Canada's Great Lakes.

- Unequal treatment of foreign and Polish-based investors, limitations of economic freedom and Poland's passive foreign investment policy are to blame for the fact that foreign investments have not reached a higher level, the foreign investors' commercial chamber representatives told the Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek at a meeting yesterday.

- The representatives of Szczecin and Gdynia shipyards, the Huta Czestochowa steelworks and the Poznan-based HCP ship engine maker are negotiating their plans to form a holding. Stocznia Szczecinska, to lead the holding, is planning to sell a 20 percent stake to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to finance the merger.
- Meeting Premiera '97 stationery and office product exhibition is starting in Warsaw today. The exhibition will last till March 1,1997.

- The state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank has produced a call for tender for supply and installation of 30 cash dispensers, the bank's spokeswoman Agnieszka Jaworska said.
- The Katowice province branch of PZU, Poland's biggest insurance firm, cut the optional driving insurance policy rates (AC) by 20 percent in the second half of February, PZU said.
- The Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy (BH) has received a credit worth 100 million European Currency Units (ECU) from the European Investment Bank to finance small size investments in Poland.
- Poland's Competiton and Consumer Protection Office has permitted the listed FarmFood food processing firm to acquire a 55 percent stake in the Tarnow-based Miestar meat processing plant.
- Infor publishing will start issuing Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki daily to replace Nowa Europa and Gazeta Prawna newspapers as of April 7, 1997, the publishing company said.
